overview.description: Ino-Shika-Cho (猪鹿蝶 - Boar, Deer, Butterfly) is the most iconic scoring combination ('Yaku') in the Japanese Hanafuda game Koi-Koi. It has also evolved into its own simplified sub-game played with Hanafuda cards, where players focus specifically on gathering these three 'Tane' (animal/object) cards to win the round.
overview.originName: 日本 (Nihon), origin of Hanafuda and Koi-Koi.

history.origins: Derived from Koi-Koi rules. The phrase 'Ino-shika-cho' is a cultural meme in Japan, representing luck and powerful combined forces.
timeline: Edo Period: Hanafuda cards develop as a gambling alternative to banned Western cards.
Meiji Era: Koi-Koi rules standardize the Ino-Shika-Cho combination.
Present: Popularized globally through media like Naruto and Nintendo's Hanafuda apps.
history.evolution: The combination is so powerful that it often dictates the entire flow of a Koi-Koi match, leading players to pursue it as a primary objective.
history.cultural: Symbolizes the harmony of nature (Boar/Bush Clover, Deer/Maple, Butterfly/Peony).

setup.dealing: 8 cards to each player, 8 cards face-up on the 'field'.

rules.objective: Capture the Boar (July), Deer (October), and Butterfly (June) cards from the field.
rules.gameplay:
1. Match a card in hand with a card in the field of the same 'month' (suit).
2. If a match is made, the player takes both cards to their scoring area.
3. **Koi-Koi**: If a player completes a combination (like Ino-Shika-Cho), they can say 'Koi-Koi' to continue for more points, or stop to win the round.
4. If the opponent completes a combination before you stop, you lose all points for that round.
keyRules: Match by month (suit): only a card of the same month can capture a table card.
If no match from hand, discard one card face-up to the table.
After play or discard, draw one card; if it matches a table card, capture; else it stays on the table.

Completing Ino-Shika-Cho (Boar, Deer, Butterfly) or another yaku lets you stop to score or call Koi-Koi to continue; if opponent forms a yaku before you do after Koi-Koi, they score double and you score nothing for the round.

strategy.basic: Identify the June, July, and October suits in the field early. If you have a card from those months in hand, wait until the 'Animal' card appears in the field to match it.
strategy.intermediate: Blocking: If your opponent has two of the three cards (e.g., Boar and Butterfly), you must prioritize capturing ANY card of the October suit to prevent them from getting the Deer.
strategy.advanced: Risk assessment: Calculating whether to call 'Koi-Koi' after getting Ino-Shika-Cho. If your opponent has many Ribbons or Scrolls, they might finish their own Yaku before you can get more points.
tips: The 'Animal' cards (Tane) are the middle tier of cards (10 points each).
Peony (June), Bush Clover (July), and Maple (October) are the critical months.

difficulty.medium: Prioritizes animal cards; calls 'Koi-Koi' too aggressively.

play_card.description: Match a card from hand with a card on the table of the same month (suit), taking both to your point pile; if no match, discard one card face-up to the table. Then draw one card from the draw pile and place it face-up; if it matches a table card, take both; otherwise the drawn card stays on the table. If three cards of the same month are on the table and you play the fourth, take all four.
play_card.constraints: You must match by month (suit). If your hand card matches a table card, you may capture that pair. If your hand card matches two table cards, you choose which to capture. If no match, you must discard one card to the table. After playing or discarding, you must draw one card; if the drawn card matches a table card you must capture; otherwise it remains on the table.

edgeCases.text: If your played card matches two table cards, you choose which to capture.
If three cards of the same month are on the table and you play the fourth, you take all four.
Oya-Ken: if both players run out of cards without either forming a yaku on the last play, the dealer (oya) scores one point and remains dealer for the next hand.
If a drawn card matches a table card, you must capture; you cannot leave it on the table.

engine.handRankingSystem: Yaku combinations (e.g. Ino-Shika-Cho: Boar, Deer, Butterfly; five Tane; ribbons); no poker hand rankings.
engine.deckDescription: Hanafuda deck of 48 cards in twelve month suits; Ino-Shika-Cho uses the three Tane (animal) cards: Boar (Bush Clover, July), Deer (Maple, October), and Butterfly (Peony, June) as the scoring combination.
engine.suitDescription: Twelve month suits (January through December); each month has four cards. Ino-Shika-Cho focuses on the Bush Clover (July), Maple (October), and Peony (June) months for the Boar, Deer, and Butterfly cards.
engine.rankDescription: Cards are grouped by month and type (Bright, Animal/Tane, Ribbon, Chaff). Ino-Shika-Cho uses the 10-point Tane cards: Boar (July), Deer (October), and Butterfly (June) as the three named targets.
engine.dealPattern: Eight cards to each player face-down, eight cards to the table face-up; remainder forms the draw pile. Often dealt in batches of two or four cards at a time.
